scope: Source selection and provisional reference preparation; existing experiments and website unchanged.
counting_note: Count source reports, not independent patients or visits. B04 and B19 include maternal/newborn material; B17 is one man with three vascular episodes; B18 is one child and family followed over time. Preparation IDs do not change the existing 33-case catalogue.

existing_catalogue.duplicate_method: Compared canonical source DOI/URL and reviewed presentation, patient history and treatment context. Topic similarity alone was not classified as duplication.
existing_catalogue.patient_overlap_review: Reviewed presentation, age, sex, clinical history and treatment context for B13–B22 against the original 33 and B01–B12, and within this completion batch; no apparent duplicate patient identified. Multiple episodes/visits within one report remain one case.

cases.brief_title: Generalised oedema during cancer treatment
cases.article_title: Amivantamab-associated capillary leak syndrome presenting with severe anasarca and profound hypoalbuminaemia in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A woman in her early 70s with metastatic lung cancer developed rapidly progressive oedema and falling albumin after starting amivantamab. The report documents investigations for competing causes and subsequent improvement after withdrawal and supportive treatment.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Preserve the treatment–symptom sequence and the alternative-cause work-up. The authors describe probable drug-associated capillary leak; they explicitly acknowledge that a definitive diagnosis was not established. Confirm the evidence needed before attributing the syndrome to treatment.

cases.brief_title: Severe low glucose after kidney–pancreas transplantation
cases.article_title: Single-strength trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (TMP/SMX)-induced hypoglycaemia in a post kidney-pancreas transplant patient
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A man in his 30s developed weakness and dizziness after prophylactic trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole was restarted. Home glucose readings were 28, 33 and 36 mg/dL on consecutive days. Kidney function was stable, but blood samples were not taken during the symptomatic episodes.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Review medication changes and acknowledge severe measured hypoglycaemia. Do not describe the home readings as simultaneous laboratory glucose/insulin/C-peptide results. Confirm appropriate urgent advice, alternative explanations and the limits of attributing the mechanism to the medicine.

cases.brief_title: Long-lasting diarrhoea and severe weight loss
cases.article_title: Olmesartan-associated enteropathy presenting as severe malnutrition
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A woman in her late 70s had 14 months of watery diarrhoea, a 32% weight loss and repeated assessments. Her combination antihypertensive products shared an ingredient that was overlooked. The record includes villous injury, negative coeliac testing and temporary improvement during admissions.

source_locations.description: laboratory, diet and biopsy context, p-13–p-19

cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Check the active ingredients across brand-name changes. Interpret coeliac serology with the diet at the time of sampling. The earlier and later negative panels were obtained under different dietary conditions. Confirm which medication and nutritional questions are essential before assessment.

cases.brief_title: Neurological symptoms around childbirth
cases.article_title: Severe maternal and neonatal hyponatraemia following excessive oral fluid intake during labour
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A first-time mother in her 30s developed slowing and incoherent speech around delivery. Her newborn subsequently had a seizure. Sodium was 111 mmol/L in the mother and 118 mmol/L in the newborn. The mother later reported substantial oral water intake during labour.

source_locations.description: sodium correction and fluid history, p-13–p-14

cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Keep the mother’s and newborn’s measurements separate. Maternal symptoms preceded postpartum oxytocin. The report records maternal sodium rising from 111 to 131 mmol/L within 12 hours and discusses concern about overcorrection. Confirm urgent assessment, monitoring and safe management expectations; do not copy the reported regimen into a universal treatment rule.

cases.brief_title: Very low platelets after hip surgery
cases.article_title: Profound thrombocytopenia and transient leucoerythroblastosis following hip fracture surgery
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A man in his 80s received heparin around hip surgery. By postoperative day 6 his platelets were 5 × 10⁹/L. Antibody testing was strongly positive, the initial platelet-activation result was inconclusive, and thromboses were subsequently identified.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Reconstruct the exposure and platelet timeline. Distinguish an inconclusive functional assay from a negative result. Confirm how the combined clinical and laboratory evidence should guide urgent specialist review; the later specialised assay findings should not be assumed available at the initial decision point.

cases.brief_title: Worsening headache and forehead swelling in a teenager
cases.article_title: Pott’s puffy tumour in a healthy adolescent following sinus barotrauma from underwater training
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A teenage boy developed worsening headache, fever and forehead/periorbital swelling after sinus symptoms and repeated underwater training. He deteriorated despite earlier assessments and oral antibiotics. Subsequent imaging identified a frontal subperiosteal abscess without intracranial extension.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Confirm deterioration/red flags and the required escalation. Treat underwater exposure as a possible contributor, not proven causation. The antibiotic accounts differ between the presentation and treatment sections; reconcile this before using an exact antibiotic sequence as a scoring requirement.

cases.brief_title: Cholestasis with a large liver cyst
cases.article_title: Obstructive cholestasis without biliary dilatation from a hepatic cyst
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A man in his 70s had pain, dark urine and cholestatic blood tests. Aspiration of a large liver cyst gave partial improvement, but symptoms and cyst enlargement recurred. Repeated imaging showed no biliary duct dilatation.

source_locations.description: repeat blood tests and imaging, p-7

cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Integrate the biochemical pattern, anatomy and response over time. Avoid equating absent duct dilatation with exclusion of obstruction. The proposed compression mechanism is an interpretation rather than a directly measured event. Confirm the differential and further information needed before deciding on intervention.

cases.brief_title: Severe gastrointestinal bleeding after neurosurgery
cases.article_title: Gastroduodenal artery pseudoaneurysm presenting as severe upper gastrointestinal bleeding in an adolescent: transarterial embolisation
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: An adolescent boy developed abdominal pain after neurosurgery and prescribed NSAID use. He returned with melaena, syncope, hypotension and tachycardia. CT did not locate a pseudoaneurysm, and an adherent clot limited endoscopic visualisation. Angiography later identified the bleeding lesion.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Confirm escalation and investigation priorities when bleeding remains unexplained. Do not claim that NSAIDs definitively caused the vascular lesion. If numerical trends are used, clarify the reported haemoglobin measurements and their timing before setting an expected calculation.

cases.brief_title: New cranial nerve symptoms in a patient with EGPA
cases.article_title: Multiple cranial neuropathies in a patient with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A man in his 60s with longstanding asthma, sinus disease, eosinophilia and a previous clinical EGPA diagnosis developed facial pain, facial weakness and visual symptoms. Imaging was re-reviewed, revealing previously unrecognised meningeal abnormalities; symptoms and imaging subsequently progressed.

source_locations.description: new symptoms and imaging review, p-5–p-7

cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Preserve the distinction between the established historical diagnosis and the explanation of new neurological findings. Keep the original MRI report separate from its later reinterpretation. Confirm essential neurological/visual assessments, competing explanations and the urgency appropriate to the chosen decision point.

cases.brief_title: Late pain in prosthetic knees after bladder treatment
cases.article_title: Late-onset Mycobacterium bovis prosthetic knee infection following intravesical BCG therapy
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A man in his late 60s developed knee pain roughly 16 months after intravesical BCG treatment and three years after knee replacements. Routine cultures and acid-fast staining were negative, but delayed culture and genotyping identified the organism. He lacked prominent systemic symptoms.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Check remote treatment history and test type/timing. Synovial cell-count details were unavailable, rather than normal. Confirm appropriate diagnostic requests and how to present this selected non-operative course without treating it as routine management for every prosthetic infection.

cases.brief_title: Persistent vomiting after initially denying medication use
cases.article_title: Emerging risks of health optimisation: refractory nausea associated with peptide injections reported to contain retatrutide
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A woman in her mid-20s had persistent nausea and vomiting despite repeated care. She initially denied medication use. Explicit, non-judgemental questioning later elicited escalating wellness injections reportedly containing retatrutide. Their composition and concentration were unverified.

source_locations.description: disclosure and unknown product details, p-13–p-16

cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Distinguish the reported product from verified exposure. Syringe units cannot establish a milligram dose without concentration. Confirm equivalent exposure questions and appropriate uncertainty. The presentation mentions loose stools, while the differential later refers to absent diarrhoea; do not silently turn this into a confirmed negative finding.

cases.brief_title: Recurrent dangerous arrhythmias and abnormal thyroid tests
cases.article_title: Refractory amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis causing malignant arrhythmias, treated with therapeutic plasma exchange-bridged thyroidectomy
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A man in his mid-60s with severe cardiac disease and amiodarone exposure developed thyrotoxicosis and recurrent ventricular arrhythmias. Investigations gave mixed subtype clues, and arrhythmias recurred despite treatment. The report describes subsequent multidisciplinary intervention and follow-up.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Interpret thyroid findings with treatment timing: scintigraphy followed a week of carbimazole. Confirm the degree of subtype certainty and escalation required. The scan caption mentions nodular goitre, while the ultrasound description reports no nodules; retain this distinction rather than assigning a definite structural diagnosis.

cases.brief_title: New liver lesions during lymphoma treatment
cases.article_title: Malignant histiocytic neoplasm with dendritic differentiation via transdifferentiation of B-cell lymphoma
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A man in his 80s with follicular lymphoma developed high-grade B-cell lymphoma and later new liver lesions. Different lesions showed different responses and biopsy findings. Liver pathology supported a histiocytic neoplasm with dendritic differentiation; subsequent biopsy also identified relapsed B-cell lymphoma.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Keep imaging suspicion separate from the tissue diagnosis of each lesion. Initial follicular-lymphoma clonality testing was not completed. Confirm acceptable pathological terminology and the strength of the lineage-change interpretation; do not require an exact rare subtype or undisclosed biopsy result at an earlier decision point.

cases.brief_title: Restricted hip movement followed by postoperative kidney injury
cases.article_title: Atraumatic iliopsoas heterotopic ossification with postoperative atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A woman in her late 40s had progressive restriction of hip movement and an ossified iliopsoas mass without reported trauma. After excision, she developed oliguria, haemolytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia and severe kidney injury on postoperative day 3. The authors diagnosed atypical haemolytic uraemic syndrome.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Treat the original mass and postoperative systemic illness as separate decision points in one patient. Complement genetic analysis and anti-factor H antibody testing were unavailable. Confirm the diagnostic alternatives and escalation requirements; postoperative timing alone does not establish a proven surgical or genetic cause.

cases.brief_title: Visual deterioration years after thyroid surgery
cases.article_title: Thyroid eye disease with dysthyroid optic neuropathy 15 years after incomplete thyroidectomy
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A woman in her late 70s developed proptosis, diplopia and impaired colour vision 15 years after intended total thyroidectomy. Investigations identified functioning residual thyroid tissue. Visual function deteriorated during treatment, followed by orbital decompression and later completion thyroidectomy.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: An intended total thyroidectomy is not proof that no thyroid tissue remains. Confirm visual red flags and the urgency of specialist assessment. Tocilizumab and orbital surgery overlapped, limiting attribution of benefit to either intervention alone; completion thyroidectomy occurred later and should not be presented as the immediate treatment of visual decline.

cases.brief_title: Persistent scrotal inflammation in Crohn’s disease
cases.article_title: Necrotising granulomatous epididymo-orchitis in the setting of Crohn’s disease
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A man in his early 50s with longstanding Crohn’s disease had recurrent epididymo-orchitis and collections despite surgery and prolonged antibiotics. Several bacterial cultures were positive, while targeted investigations did not establish a granulomatous infection. Pathology review suggested a possible extraintestinal manifestation; symptoms resolved after a change in biologic treatment.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Do not turn selected negative tests into “all cultures were negative”. Fresh cultures were not sent from one later procedure. Confirm how infection and inflammatory explanations should be weighed, and what evidence is needed before attributing the persistent disease to Crohn’s.

cases.brief_title: New vascular symptoms across decades
cases.article_title: Metachronous dural arteriovenous fistulas in a single patient: a 25-year evolution of three distinct lesions
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: One man developed three dural arteriovenous fistulas at different sites over a long follow-up. Initial tinnitus and headache, later scalp changes and transient neurological symptoms, and a subsequent new episode led to separate assessments. The first two lesions were treated; the third was monitored.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Count one patient, not three independent cases. Distinguish new lesions from recurrence at the same site. Preserve the explicit dates and rounded intervals without inventing exact onset dates. Confirm which anatomical and drainage features justify intervention or observation at each decision point.

cases.brief_title: Parenting concerns at a child’s routine visit
cases.article_title: Two-year outcomes and feedback after a parenting assessment is integrated into primary care
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A mother brought her three-year-old son with anxiety, poor sleep and behavioural concerns. A parenting assessment prompted counselling and a handbook, later shared with the father. Assessment scores improved at later visits; interviews described changes in parenting and child behaviour.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: This source suits a parent-facing counselling task rather than requiring a rare diagnosis. An elevated screen does not itself diagnose abuse. Confirm appropriate questions, support and communication expectations. Reported improvement in one selected family does not isolate the effect of counselling from maturation, other information or reporting bias.

cases.brief_title: Persistent caesarean-scar pain in preterm pregnancy
cases.article_title: Uterine torsion with concurrent uterine dehiscence in the third trimester of pregnancy
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A woman in her late 20s with two previous caesareans presented at 28+4 weeks with localised scar pain. She was stable, but ultrasound assessment was limited and MRI was inconclusive. Worsening symptoms preceded delivery at 30+5 weeks, when uterine torsion and a separate scar dehiscence were identified.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Keep antenatal suspicion separate from the later operative diagnoses. Inconclusive imaging did not exclude structural disease. Confirm monitoring and escalation expectations at the chosen time; do not require prediction of an undisclosed operative finding or convert this individual timing of delivery into a universal rule.

cases.brief_title: New tumour findings after prolonged imatinib response
cases.article_title: Progression of advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumour after over 20-year response to imatinib
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A woman diagnosed with metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumour after pathology review received imatinib from 2002. After prolonged response, changing CT findings led to biopsy-confirmed recurrence in 2023. Later progression prompted another systemic treatment. Molecular testing was performed on the recurrent tumour.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Distinguish original pathology, later mutation testing and changing imaging technique. A mutation interpreted as an original driver was not verified in the original specimen. Confirm when new findings warrant reassessment and how strongly the available molecular evidence supports the proposed disease trajectory.

cases.brief_title: Unexpected anatomy during hernia repair
cases.article_title: Duplicated spermatic cord encountered during inguinal hernia repair
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A man in his 60s underwent elective repair of a reducible inguinal hernia. Two spermatic cord structures were unexpectedly found during surgery. The operative plan was modified to preserve them, and postoperative ultrasound documented the reported duplication and vascular flow.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: This source particularly suits operative-record review. Ultrasound images could not be exported; the authors rely on the official report. Confirm anatomical terminology and safety expectations before grading. Do not require a model to anticipate an undisclosed incidental variant, or to request information outside the opportunities of the task.

cases.brief_title: Scrotal swelling initially labelled hydrocele
cases.article_title: Primary malignant mesothelioma of the tunica vaginalis presenting as hydrocele: imaging pitfalls
cases.access: publisher full text verified in browser
cases.case_summary: A man in his late 70s had painless scrotal swelling initially reported as uncomplicated hydrocele. Surgery revealed unexpected nodules. Histology and ancillary testing supported malignant mesothelioma of the tunica vaginalis, followed by specialist discussion and surveillance.
cases.provisional_clinical_reference: Separate the original scan report from later interpretation. The prose describes retrospective subtle nodularity, while Figure 2’s caption says no mural nodularity; resolve this before using it as a scoring fact. Confirm appropriate reassessment and management options without treating this individual surveillance decision as the standard for all patients.
